tools.description: Passively inspect one Electron renderer page (a hostless file:// page) over CDP: frame origins, a DOM summary, parsed scripts (optionally their sources) and, opt-in, console entries. Never navigates or evaluates; values are never kept.

target_id.description: The renderer target id (from js_electron_pages_list); the first renderer otherwise.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_electron_pages_list
tools.description: List the debuggable targets of an Electron app started with --remote-debugging-port (loopback), labelling renderer pages (file:// or app:// URLs) and other targets. Attach-only discovery over HTTP.

cdp_endpoint.description: Loopback CDP endpoint of the Electron app (it must be started with --remote-debugging-port).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_electron_walkthrough_record
tools.description: Launch an Electron app's own executable with a private profile and a loopback debugging port, run a short script (wait / reload / navigate / click) against its first renderer, capture network request outlines, then terminate the owned process. Executes the app and accesses the network, so it needs your approval.

application_executable.description: Absolute path of the Electron app's executable to launch.

args.description: Extra arguments passed to the app after the debugging flags.

startup_secs.description: Seconds to wait for the app to start its debugging port.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_exports_compare
tools.description: Compare what each module exports (ES module names, CommonJS names, the kind of module.exports) between two application graphs, matching modules by path then by structure.

left.description: The older version: js_app_map evidence or an absolute path.

right.description: The newer version, in the same forms.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_function_explain
tools.description: Function-level slice of an application graph: for the seeded functions, their calls (resolved where possible), callers (resolved or same-name inferred), strings, the IPC/effects/endpoints/storage they touch, and a depth-limited callee tree. Unresolved dynamic calls are listed.

application.description: js_app_map evidence or an absolute path to analyse.

oneOf.description: Case-insensitive substring.

value.description: What to look for: a channel name, function name, string, module path, URL fragment or node id.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_runtime_code_match
tools.description: Match app graph evidence against what was seen running (captured scripts with URLs and sha256): each static module is loaded, resident in a loaded bundle, loaded with different content, not observed, or unknown; runtime-only scripts are listed. Pure computation over evidence.

runtime_evidence.description: Runtime evidence that lists scripts (objects with `url` and `sha256`), inline or retained.

static_evidence.description: The static side: one or more application graphs.

evidence.description: js_app_map evidence (inline or {"kind":"saved","evidence_id":...}) or an absolute path.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_runtime_watch
tools.description: Attach the V8 inspector to one Node/Electron target and observe passively: it sends exactly Runtime.enable and Debugger.enable, then records the scripts parsed (deduplicated and sorted), execution contexts and a parse-failure count. Never resumes a paused (--inspect-brk) target. runtime_kind is taken as given.

runtime_kind.description: The kind of runtime, as given (not checked).

target_id.description: The target id to observe (from js_runtimes_list); the first otherwise.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_runtimes_list
tools.description: List the inspectable targets of a Node or Electron process started with --inspect (loopback V8 inspector endpoint), with their ids and whether another client is attached. Attach-only discovery.

cdp_endpoint.description: Loopback V8 inspector endpoint, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:9229 (node --inspect=127.0.0.1:9229).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_source_bundle_compare
tools.description: Match reference source files (from app_source_import, or a folder path) to the shipped app's files and bundle modules by path, source-map listing, shared strings, function names and export names; reports matches with scores and reasons, unmatched sources and bundle code without a source.

application.description: js_app_map evidence or an absolute path to analyse.

source.description: app_source_import evidence (inline or retained) or an absolute source folder path.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_source_locate
tools.description: Map a position in generated (bundled/minified) JavaScript back to its original file, line, column and name through a source map (a .map file, a script's sourceMappingURL, or an inline data: map). Lines are 1-based, columns 0-based UTF-16. Returns every original position at that point and nearby original source when the map embeds it.

context_lines.description: Original-source lines of context around each hit.

script_path.description: Or the generated script: its sourceMappingURL (a sibling file or an inline data: URL) is followed.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__js_sources_restore
tools.description: Turn minified bundles back into readable files in a new folder: split webpack/esbuild/browserify module tables into one file per module, pretty-print everything, apply safe unminify rewrites (!0→true, void 0→undefined, statement sequences, webpack module parameter names via scope analysis) and write original files embedded in source maps. manifest.json records every input digest, module byte range and output file, and says when its path or entry budget left originals out.

additional_paths.description: Up to 16 more scripts or folders.

limit.description: Output files listed per page in the result.

output_directory.description: Absolute path of a folder that does not exist yet.

path.description: Absolute path of a script or a folder of scripts.

oneOf.description: Split only recognised bundle module tables; pretty-print everything; write source-map originals.
Pretty-print only (no splitting, no source-map originals).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__managed_app_graph_build
tools.description: Project a .NET assembly (managed evidence or a path) into an application graph: assembly, referenced assemblies, types, methods, external members, native modules and resources, joined by contains, references, inherits, calls and pinvoke edges. Bounded by max_nodes.

input.description: Managed evidence (managed_assembly_show, managed_members_list or managed_native_calls_list) or an absolute path; the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__managed_assemblies_compare
tools.description: Compare the members of two assemblies (managed_members_list evidence or absolute paths) with tiered unique matching: identical IL and signature (survives renames), then type+name+signature, then the same structure. Reports unchanged, changed (body differs), renamed or moved, added, removed and ambiguous methods, plus added/removed types and fields.

left.description: The older build: managed_members_list evidence (inline, {"kind":"saved","evidence_id":...} or an id) or an absolute path.

right.description: The newer build, in the same forms.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__managed_assembly_show
tools.description: Built-in ECMA-335 reader: PE/CLI header (runtime version, IL-only/32-bit/strong-name flags, entry point, ReadyToRun), metadata streams and table row counts, assembly identity, assembly and module references, manifest resources, forwarded types, assembly attributes (TargetFramework decoded) and a classification (runtime family, implementation, managed architecture). Uses the active target unless path is given.

path.description: Absolute path of a .NET assembly (.dll/.exe); the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__managed_ilspy_decompile
tools.description: Decompile a .NET assembly (absolute path or the active target) with the installed ILSpy command line (ilspycmd): operation decompile gives C# for the whole assembly, or for one type with type_name (`Namespace.Type`, nested types as `Outer+Inner`); il gives the whole assembly's IL; list_types lists its classes, interfaces, structs, delegates and enums. Its update check is turned off, so it never goes online. Returns the raw text paged by lines. Optional engine: the built-in .NET tools need nothing installed.

offset.description: First output line of the page.

path.description: Absolute path of the assembly; the active target when omitted.

type_name.description: For decompile: one fully qualified type (`Namespace.Type`, nested as `Outer+Inner`).

oneOf.description: C# source.
The IL, for the whole assembly.
Every class, interface, struct, delegate and enum, one per line.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__managed_members_list
tools.description: Types, fields, properties, events and methods of a .NET assembly with C#-like signatures; for each IL method body: header kind, max stack, locals, exception clauses, IL size, il_hash, an il_shape_hash that survives renames, call targets, field accesses and string literals (optionally the IL listing). Filter with type_names; paged by type (offset/limit).

path.description: Absolute path of a .NET assembly; the active target when omitted.

type_names.description: Only these types (full name like `Ns.Type`, nested as `Ns.Outer/Inner`, or simple name).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__managed_native_calls_list
tools.description: Where a .NET assembly crosses into native code: P/Invoke (DllImport) rows with module, entry point, charset, calling convention, SetLastError, best-fit and PreserveSig; internal calls; native-code (mixed-mode) and runtime-implemented methods; UnmanagedCallersOnly and LibraryImport declarations; module references and vtable fixups.

path.description: Absolute path of a .NET assembly (.dll/.exe); the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__managed_native_calls_verify
tools.description: Check each P/Invoke of a managed assembly (managed_native_calls_list evidence or a path) against the exports of native libraries (native_layout_show evidence or absolute paths): found, found as an A/W or stdcall-decorated variant, case mismatch, missing, or undetermined when the module wasn't supplied.

managed.description: The managed side: managed_native_calls_list evidence or an absolute assembly path.

native.description: Native libraries: native_layout_show evidence or absolute paths (ELF, PE or Mach-O).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__managed_reconstruction_check
tools.description: Check user-supplied C# (a file, a folder of .cs files, or text) against the assembly's member evidence: declarations matched, signature mismatches, members missing from the source, extra source members, compiler-implicit members, and missing/extra types. Declarations only, not behaviour.

max_files.description: Most .cs files read from a folder.

members.description: The assembly: managed_members_list evidence or an absolute path.

source_path.description: Absolute path of a .cs file or a folder of .cs files.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_address_offset_show
tools.description: Map a virtual address to its offset in the original file (and the section holding it).

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_address_show
tools.description: The name, containing function, comment, inline comment and bookmarks at one address in the active target. Each facet is a value or a clear 'unavailable' with a reason.

document.description: Target id or name; the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_api_show
tools.description: The system and library APIs a function calls, grouped by purpose (files, network, processes, crypto...), plus internal calls, indirect calls and jump tables.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

function.description: Function name or address.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_bookmark_add
tools.description: Bookmark an address with an optional name.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

name.description: Bookmark label.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_bookmark_remove
tools.description: Remove the bookmark at an address.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_bookmarks_show
tools.description: Bookmarks you or an agent set on the active target.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_bytes_find
tools.description: Find every place a byte signature or a piece of text occurs in a file (an absolute path, or the active target). `pattern` is hex byte pairs with `??` for any byte (spaces optional, e.g. `48 8B ?? 24`); `text` is searched as UTF-8 and/or UTF-16LE. Matches are ordered by file offset and paged (offset/limit); for ELF, PE and Mach-O programs each match also carries its virtual address and containing section when the bytes are mapped. Overlapping matches are all reported. At most 100000 matches are retained, in file-offset order across all queries.

document.description: Open document (id or name) to search instead of the active one; ignored with path.

encoding.description: How `text` is encoded in the file: utf8, utf16le or both (default).

path.description: Absolute path of the file to search; the active target when omitted.

pattern.description: Hex byte pairs with `??` wildcards, e.g. "48 8B ?? 24 ?? 00".

oneOf.description: Both UTF-8 and UTF-16LE (default).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_bytes_show
tools.description: Bytes at a virtual address as hex (default 256, at most 65536), never past the end of the section.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_call_graph_show
tools.description: Callees (forward) or callers (backward) of a function, level by level, with edges and honest truncation.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_call_path_find
tools.description: Shortest direct-call path from one function to another (forward or backward), with goal status and residual unknowns. Forward, the goal may also be an import (e.g. CreateWindowExW): the path ends at the call to it.

direction.description: forward (start calls ... goal, default) or backward (goal is reached from start's callers).

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

goal.description:
Goal function (name or address), or an import's name when tracing forward; without it,
everything reachable is listed.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_call_site_resolve
tools.description: Resolve the target(s) of one call or jump site: direct target, import, jump-table candidates, or unresolved.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_comment_read
tools.description: The comment at an address, or null.

address.description: Virtual address (0x-hex); the cursor when omitted.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_comment_write
tools.description: Set the comment at an address (empty clears it) and read it back.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_crash_show
tools.description: Read a Linux ELF core dump: the signal and its meaning, the faulting address, registers of each thread, the process name and arguments, mapped files, and which file the crash happened in.

path.description: Absolute path of an ELF core file; the active target when omitted.

with_debugger_context.description: Ask for live debugger context (not available in clean-room mode; reported as a limitation).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_cursor_address_show
tools.description: The cursor address in the active document (set with native_cursor_goto or in the app).

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_cursor_back
tools.description: The address of the previous instruction (in code) or previous byte (in data) before an address (the cursor by default). Doesn't move the cursor.

address.description: Virtual address (0x-hex); the cursor when omitted.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_cursor_forward
tools.description: The address of the next instruction (in code) or next byte (in data) after an address (the cursor by default). Doesn't move the cursor.

address.description: Virtual address (0x-hex); the cursor when omitted.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_cursor_function_show
tools.description: The function containing the cursor.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_cursor_goto
tools.description: Move the cursor to an address (must be mapped in the program).

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_cursor_show
tools.description: The current cursor address in the active target.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_cutter_command_run
tools.description: Run one read-only Rizin command in a shared Cutter session (port, default 9090) and return its text, paged by lines: information (i...), printing and disassembly (p..., x...), analysis (a...), search (/...), seek (s...), flags (f...), comments (C...), types (t...) and help (?...). Writes, shell escapes, scripts, debugging, pipes and chaining are refused. Analysis and seek commands change what the Cutter window shows, as if typed in its console.

command.description: One read-only Rizin command, for example `afl`, `pdf @ main` or `iz`.

offset.description: First output line of the page.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_cutter_sessions_list

Confidence is honest: strong signals (symbols, toolchain paths, dependency data) versus weak ones (panic text alone). Built-in; never runs the program.

tools.description: Summarize a saved pcap or pcapng capture with the built-in decoder (nothing installed): format, interfaces and link types, packet and byte counts, time span, frames per protocol, busiest addresses, conversations (flows) with packets and bytes in each direction and the application protocols seen (paged), DNS questions and answers, HTTP/1.x requests (method, Host, target; credentials removed) and TLS ClientHello server names (SNI) and ALPN. tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_approvals_set
tools.description: Choose, for one kind of builder action in a project, whether it goes ahead (`allow`), waits for the person's OK on a card (`ask`) or is refused (`refuse`); `default` follows Auto mode. Kinds: `web` (reading websites, searching), `commands` (outside the usual build commands), `outside_files` (changing files outside the project), `publish` (git push, npm publish, gh pr create...), `delete_outside`, `system` (system changes and files, Craft Anything's own records), `other_tools`. With no kind, says what every kind gets now. Takes effect from the builder's next action, also mid-build. Only the person changes these: an agent's call may only make a kind stricter.

kind.description: The kind of action (`publish`, `web`...); none just reads what every kind gets.

ActionKind.description:
A kind of builder action that asks for approval, which a project can decide about ahead of time
(`Manifest::approvals`).

oneOf.description: Reading websites and searching the web.
Commands outside the usual build commands.
Changing files outside the project.
Pushing to a git server or publishing anywhere (`git push`, `npm publish`, `gh pr create`...).
Deleting anything outside the project or the temp folder.
Changing the system, its settings or users, system files, or Craft Anything's own records.
Tools with no rule of their own.

ApprovalChoice.description: What one kind of a project's builder actions should get.

oneOf.description: What Auto mode gives it.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_build_finish

Everything so far is kept, and a new message carries on from here. It doesn't stop a build that is still running: pause it first.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_delete
tools.description: Delete a project: everything Craft Anything made in its folder (its records, checks, and what was built in app/). The person's own files stay (an app edited in place, the files a project started from). Can't be undone, so `confirm` must be true; stop a build first.

confirm.description: Must be true: deleting can't be undone.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_duplicate
tools.description: Copy a project beside it under a new name, to try something else from where it is: what was built, the pictures of the original and the study come along; the conversation, questions and usage don't, and neither do dependencies or compiler output (the next build makes them again). An app edited in place is copied into the copy's app/ folder.

name.description: The copy's name (default: "<name> copy").

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_inbox_answer
tools.description: Answer a question or approval a project is waiting on (an id from project_show): a choice or text for questions, allow (and always) for approvals. The answer reaches a running build at once and is kept in the project's conversation.

always.description: Allow this kind of action for the rest of the project (approvals).

text.description: A typed answer (questions), or a reason (approvals).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_list
tools.description: List the projects in every project folder from settings (where new projects go, then `project_folders`), or in one folder, newest first: name, folder, app folder, request, target, stack, status, the latest check and how many questions are waiting.

projects_dir.description: Only this folder (default: every project folder from settings).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_open_folder
tools.description: Open the project's folder (or its app/ folder) in the file manager, or one of its pinned builds' folders.

app.description: Open the app/ folder (what was built) instead of the project folder.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_pin_create
tools.description: Keep the project's current build at hand to open later, whatever the builder changes next. `frozen` (the default) copies the app's files and its program into the project's pinned/ folder, without compiler output or dependencies it doesn't start from, so rebuilds can't change or break it. `light` copies the program and the code too but hard-links dependencies and media to the project's, saving their space: replacing or deleting those in the project leaves the pin's as they were, but a file rewritten in place changes in both. With `estimate`, only says what each would take. Websites can't be pinned yet.

estimate.description: Only say what each kind of copy would take; pin nothing.

mode.description:
`frozen` (default): a copy of its own; `light`: shares dependencies and media with the
project. `live` was retired and is refused.

name.description: Its name (default: the project's name and round).

PinMode.description: How a pin keeps its build.

oneOf.description: Its own copy of the build, which nothing else changes (the default).
Its own program and code, sharing dependencies and media with the project.

The project's app where it is, as the latest build left it. No longer made (it only
opened what Play opens); pins already saved this way still work.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_pin_delete
tools.description: Remove a pin. Its copy goes with it, including anything the program saved beside itself there, so `confirm` must be true; a running pin is refused until it's stopped.

confirm.description: Must be true: a pin's copy, and what it saved, can't be brought back.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_pin_open
tools.description: Start a pinned build in its own window. If it's already running, says so instead of starting a second copy, unless `another` is true (copies of one pin share the files they save beside themselves). A start that quits within two seconds is reported with its exit code and last output. It runs the code the builder wrote, so it needs the person's consent.

another.description: Start another copy even if one is running.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_pin_rename
tools.description: Give a pin a new name.

name.description: Its new name.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_pin_stop
tools.description: Close what a pin started in this session (every copy of it).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_pins_list
tools.description: The pins of one project, or of every project in the project folders from settings: id, name, frozen or light, the round it was pinned at, its size, and whether it's running (started in this session).

project.description: Only this project's pins (default: every project's).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_plan_fold
tools.description: Fold the builder's plan card away (#504). The steps stay in the project's conversation, and a later run's plan shows again. Call it between builds: a build saves its conversation as it goes, so a fold made during one can be overwritten by that build's next save.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_play
tools.description: Start the finished game or app a project built (its program, a Unity or Unreal package, or a Godot project in Godot), in its own window. If it's already running, says so instead of starting a second copy, unless `another` is true. A start that quits within two seconds is reported with its exit code and last output. It runs the code the builder wrote, so it needs the person's consent. Websites use project_preview instead. Known limit on Windows: when the caller's output is a pipe, the started program inherits it, so a caller reading that output to its end waits until the program exits (#207).

another.description: Start another copy even if one is running.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_preview
tools.description: Serve a project's built website on this computer only (loopback) and return its address. It keeps serving for this session; with `wait`, the call itself serves until it's cancelled (Ctrl+C in the CLI).

wait.description: Serve until the call is cancelled instead of returning at once (for the CLI).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_questions_set
tools.description: Choose whether the builder's questions (core_person_ask) in a project are shown to the person to answer (`ask`) or answered with "decide yourself and say what you chose" (`decide`); `default` follows the app's setting (`questions` in settings, which follows Auto mode until set). With no mode, says what applies now. Takes effect from the builder's next question, also mid-build.

mode.description: `ask`, `decide` or `default`; none just reads what applies.

QuestionsChoice.description: What a project's questions should get.

oneOf.description: The app's setting.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_rename
tools.description: Give a project a new name (its folder stays where it is).

name.description: Its new name.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_show
tools.description: One project: its request, target, stack, status, checks, questions still waiting for an answer, and its conversation (paged with offset/limit, newest last).

limit.description: Return at most this many items (default and maximum 200; the newest when no offset).

offset.description: Skip this many conversation items from the start.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__radio_decoders_list
tools.description: List the device protocols the installed rtl_433 can decode: number, name, and whether it runs by default (the others only run when asked for with decoders). Optional engine.

filter.description: Only decoders whose name contains this text (any case).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__radio_recording_decode
tools.description: Decode a saved radio recording (absolute path or the active target) with rtl_433: I/Q samples (.cu8, .cs8, .cs16, .cf32) or demodulated AM/FM (.am.s16, .fm.s16), format and sample rate read from the file name (for example g001_433.92M_250k.cu8; 250 kHz when absent) unless sample_rate is given. Returns each decoded message (device model, id, channel and readings) paged with offset/limit, plus counts by model. decoders limits decoding to those protocol numbers (see radio_decoders_list); otherwise rtl_433's default set runs. Optional engine.

decoders.description: Protocol numbers to decode (from radio_decoders_list); empty runs the default set.

path.description: Absolute path of the recording; omit to use the active target.

sample_rate.description: Sample rate in Hz, when the file name doesn't say.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_activity_show
tools.description: What a project's builds did, line by line, newest last: each stage, every command and file the builder touched and how it ended, what it said, and what programs printed outside the conversation. Secrets are hidden. Works while a build runs and after. `limit` lines (200 by default, at most 2000), `offset` lines back from the newest.

limit.description: How many lines to return (200 by default, at most 2000).

offset.description: How many lines back from the newest to end at (0 by default).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_check
tools.description: For the builder: test the project's current build against the original now, with the same checks Craft Anything runs after each turn (a website's likeness at each width with the padding, colour, font and layout differences; an app's or game's picture against the original's; whether it builds; the mechanics sheet; credits). The project's running build answers it, so the builder can fix what it lists and check again before replying. Not counted as a round. project defaults to the project this tool server works for.

project.description: The project's folder; default: the project this tool server was started for.

wait_minutes.description:
Longest wait for the result, in minutes (1..=60, default 35): a website with several pages
or a game's engine build takes a few minutes, and the run stops a check at 30.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_note
tools.description: Tell a running build something more; the agent reads it at its next step. With no build running, start a follow-up with rebuild_start instead.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_note_withdraw
tools.description: Take back a note given with rebuild_note (by the id it returned) while the agent hasn't read it yet; it returns the note's text. Once the agent has read it, it can't be taken back.

id.description: The note's id, as rebuild_note returned it.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_question_ask
tools.description: Ask a question about a project's build ("where are the latest files?", "why this engine?") without starting a build or a round, and without changing anything. Claude Code answers from a copy of the builder's own session, which isn't kept, reading files only (none in Clean room); an AI with an API key answers with the tools that change nothing. Other coding agents are refused. Safe while a build runs: it doesn't interrupt it. Returns the answer, how it was answered and its cost, and keeps it in the project (`rebuild_questions_list`).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_questions_list
tools.description: The questions asked about a project's build and their answers, oldest first (the newest 200).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_start
tools.description: Start building: a new project from a request and a target (a web address, an absolute path, or - for none), or a follow-up on an existing project. A coding agent studies, builds, checks and refines in the background; follow it with rebuild_status and project_show, answer its questions with project_inbox_answer. Up to `build.parallel` projects build at once (2 by default); more are queued and start on their own as others finish. It runs a coding agent that writes and builds code, so it needs consent.

backend.description:
The coding agent to use (an enabled backend name), kept with a new project for its later
changes; default: the one set up for building.

build_with.description: What to build with: an engine (unity, unreal, godot, rust) or a stack's full name.

existing.description:
With `project_folder` that has files and isn't a project yet: `edit` (they're the app,
edited in place) or `start_from` (material to start from; the app is built in app/ beside
them).

generate_assets.description:
For a new game: the builder may generate pictures and 3D models (paid from the person's
asset provider key, within the project's budget). Default false; change it later with
project_assets_allow.

pictures.description:
Pictures of the original (absolute paths): the look the person expects. They're copied
into the project's reference/ folder for the builder.

project.description: Continue this project folder instead of starting a new one.

project_folder.description:
Start the new project in this folder itself instead (it's added to the project list). If
it already has files, `existing` says what they are; if it already holds a project, its
saved target, settings and stack are kept and `request` becomes its follow-up.

projects_dir.description: Where a new project's folder goes (default: the projects folder from settings).

request.description:
What to make (a new project), or the follow-up message (with `project`, or a
`project_folder` that already holds one).

resume.description:
With `project`: carry on where its last run stopped (paused, or the app or the computer
stopped) instead of sending `request` as a follow-up.

rounds.description: Refinement rounds after the first build (default 2).

target.description:
For a new project: a web address, an absolute path to an app, game or file, or `-` for none.
A `project_folder` that already holds one keeps its saved target.

ExistingFiles.description: What the files already in a picked folder are to a new project.

oneOf.description: The app itself: the builder edits them in place.
Material to start from: the builder reads them and builds the app in app/ beside them.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_status
tools.description: Whether a project's build is running in this session (or queued, and where), its status and note, the latest check, and how many questions are waiting.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_stop
tools.description: Pause a project's running build. Its work so far is kept; a follow-up continues it.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_captures_compare
tools.description: Compare two runtime_walkthrough_record evidence records dimension by dimension (terminal, exit, filesystem, events) and report what changed. Pure; no program is run.

left.description: The first run: runtime_walkthrough_record evidence (inline, {"kind":"saved",...} or a bare id).

right.description: The second run, in the same forms.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_ui_read
tools.description: Read the UI tree of a running app by its pid: every window's controls in order with their depth, role, title, identifier and value (macOS: the accessibility tree, optionally with a screenshot; Windows: UI Automation, also the class, position and size, and whether it's enabled; window_id picks one window by its handle). Password fields' values are never read; long values are cut at 500 characters. Other hosts get a clear wrong_os result.

max_nodes.description: Largest number of accessibility nodes to return.

pid.description: The process id of the running app.

screenshot.description:
Include a screenshot (PNG, base64) alongside the tree. macOS 14+: captures one on-screen
window belonging to pid, restricted by window_id when supplied, at up to 2048 pixels
per side. Without window_id, captures the first matching window. Needs existing Screen
Recording permission; failures are explicit limitations and never open permission dialogs.

window_id.description: A specific window to restrict to (on Windows, its window handle).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_ui_walkthrough_record
tools.description: Run a short scripted UI walkthrough against a running app by its pid and record its UI tree before and after the steps. Each step names an action and an element (its exact title or identifier). macOS: any accessibility action (e.g. AXPress). Windows (UI Automation): press (invoke, else toggle, select or expand), expand, collapse, toggle, select or focus; AXPress, AXShowMenu and AXRaise work too. Each step reports dispatched, element_not_found, not_supported, unknown_action or failed. Password fields' titles and values are never read. Other hosts get wrong_os.

steps.description: Steps to perform, each an accessibility action such as press/focus on an element path.

action.description:
Accessibility action, e.g. `AXPress` (on Windows also press, expand, collapse, toggle,
select or focus).

element.description: Identifier or title path to the element the action targets.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_walkthrough_record
tools.description: Run a program under a terminal with a scripted timeline of typed input, resizes and signals, then record the terminal screen, exit, and (opt-in) which files changed. Values that change every run (process ids, loopback ports, 10 ms time buckets; optionally paths and literal patterns) are normalised so two runs compare. Bounded by time, output and files; the whole process group is killed on timeout or cancel. Runs code, so it needs your OK.

environment.description: Extra environment variables applied on top of the inherited environment.

executable.description: The program to run (absolute path or a name resolved on PATH).

finish_ms.description: 0 = SIGKILL at the deadline; > 0 = SIGTERM, wait this long, then SIGKILL.

normalization.description:
Make two runs comparable: replace values that change every run (on by default for process
ids, ports and 10 ms time buckets).

sandbox.description: Run inside bubblewrap if it is installed (recorded honestly either way).

watched_paths.description:
Absolute paths to snapshot before and after (opt-in). File contents are never read; only
path, size and sha256.

working_directory.description: Working directory (absolute). Defaults to the program's own default.

data.description: Text to type. A trailing newline is not added for you.

paths.description: Replace the working directory and the temp folder with <cwd> and <tmp>.

patterns.description: Literal replacements (no patterns), applied last; at most 100.

pids.description: Replace the run's process ids with <pid>.

ports.description: Replace ports after localhost, 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0 and [::1] with <port>.

time_step_ms.description: Round event dispatch times down to this many milliseconds (0 keeps them exact).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__settings_set
tools.description: Set one setting by its dotted key from settings_show (`auto_mode`, `deep_mode`, `projects_dir`, `assets.budget_usd`...) to a JSON value, then save. Unknown keys and values of the wrong type are refused, and nothing is written.

key.description: A dotted key from settings_show, e.g. `deep_mode`.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__settings_show
tools.description: The current settings as JSON (mode, Auto mode, Deep mode/Ghidra, engine paths, projects folder, asset budget and picture model, AI backends). API keys are never in settings.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__setup_apply
tools.description: Connect Craft Anything to coding-agent apps: register its MCP server in their config files (backing each up first) and install the skill. Changes other apps' files, so it asks first.

all_detected.description: Every agent app found on this computer.

clients.description: Client ids to set up (claude_code, codex, cursor...); empty refreshes the ones already set up.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__setup_doctor
tools.description: Check the install, each agent app's registration, engines, and that the MCP server answers.

clients.description: Only these clients; empty checks every detected one.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__setup_plan
tools.description: What connecting Craft Anything to coding-agent apps (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor...) would change: each config file, the lines that change, and the skill files. Writes nothing.

all_detected.description: Every agent app found on this computer.

clients.description: Client ids to set up (claude_code, codex, cursor...); empty refreshes the ones already set up.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__setup_uninstall
tools.description: Remove Craft Anything's entries and skill from every agent app's config. Changes other apps' files, so it asks first.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_browser_connect
tools.description: Attach to a loopback CDP endpoint (a browser started with --remote-debugging-port) or launch a located Chromium headless, and report the product, protocol version and debuggable target count. A quick connectivity check before the other browser tools.

cdp_endpoint.description: Loopback CDP endpoint, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:9222. Omit to launch a browser.

launch.description: Launch a located Chromium when no endpoint is given.

no_sandbox.description: Pass --no-sandbox when launching (needed in some containers).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_coverage_measure
tools.description: Turn on V8 precise coverage on one page, observe for a window, then report per-script which functions and block ranges ran (UTF-16 offsets, with call counts when available). Changes the page's profiler state and discards coverage data on stop, so it is not idempotent.

offset.description: First script of the page in the result.

watch_ms.description: How long to let code run while measuring (milliseconds, default 10s).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_listeners_list
tools.description: Resolve a CSS selector on one page and list the DOM event listeners registered on that element: event type, capture/passive/once flags and the handler's script location (URL, line, column). No handler source is read.

selector.description: A CSS selector identifying the element.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_mcp_tools_list
tools.description: Best effort: enable the experimental WebMCP CDP domain and collect any tools the page advertises (names and declared input outlines only) during a short window. The tools are never invoked. Honest when the browser does not support the domain.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_modules_trace
tools.description: Fetch the scripts a live page has loaded and build their ES module import graph: each script and the specifiers it imports, resolved to URLs where relative, with bare specifiers reported as needing an import map. Static reading of the live sources; nothing is executed.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_page_js_analyze
tools.description: Fetch the scripts a live page has loaded over CDP and run the built-in JavaScript analyser on them: chunk graph, module boundaries, routes, HTTP endpoints and vendor fingerprints. Optionally decodes inline (data:) source maps and fetches same-origin maps. Passive; nothing is executed.

load_source_maps.description: Decode inline (data:) source maps and fetch same-origin maps.

offset.description: First module of the page in the result.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_page_screenshot_take
tools.description: Capture a PNG screenshot of the current state of one page and return it inline with its sha256 (plus bytes, dimensions, base64). Passive; the page is not navigated.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_page_show
tools.description: Passively observe one page over CDP for a short window: frame origins, a DOM summary (node names/types and attribute names with value lengths only), parsed scripts (optionally their sources, each with its sha256), resources, and — each opt-in — accessibility names, console entries, network request outlines, WebSocket outlines and storage key names. Never navigates, clicks or evaluates. Cookies, auth headers and storage values are never kept; JSON bodies become outlines.

hidden_values.description: Values to redact wherever they appear (any encoding). Only the count is recorded.

target_id.description: The target id to inspect (from web_pages_list); the first page otherwise.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_page_states_capture
tools.description: On the open website, open up to max_states of its visible menus, pop-ups, tabs and collapsed sections (aria-expanded, aria-haspopup, unselected tabs, <summary>; never form controls or submit buttons) one at a time: click it, take a screenshot, record what changed (expanded, a dialog appeared, the tab or the address changed), then put the page back. Writes state-<n>.png and states.json into a new folder. Clicking runs the site's own code, so it needs your approval.

output_directory.description: Absolute path of a folder that does not exist yet; the states are written there.

width.description: Page width in CSS pixels (320..=3840, default 1440).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_page_watch
tools.description: Passively watch one page over a longer window (default 10s) and record a bounded timeline of network request outlines, console entries, WebSocket frame outlines and navigation/lifecycle events, all data-minimised. Never navigates or evaluates.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_pages_list
tools.description: List the debuggable targets (pages, workers, iframes) of a loopback CDP endpoint with their ids, kinds and origin-only URLs, plus the browser product and protocol version. Read-only discovery over HTTP; no WebSocket.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_pixels_compare
tools.description: Compare two PNG screenshots pixel by pixel with a per-channel threshold (0..255): whether they are comparable, how many pixels differ, the difference fraction, the largest channel delta and the changed bounding box. No pixel data is returned. Pure computation.

before.description: Earlier PNG: a web_page_screenshot_take evidence (inline/retained), or inline {base64} / {path}.

common_area.description:
Compare the area both images share (top-left) when their sizes differ, and add a coarse
`layout_similarity` (0..1, share of 16 px tiles with matching mean colour) and a
`perceptual_similarity` (0..1, mean SSIM of brightness: edges, text, texture). Use it to
compare a rebuild with the original page, whose heights rarely match exactly.

ignore.description:
With common_area: a noise-<width>.png mask from web_site_capture ({path} or {base64});
its white squares (parts that change by themselves) are left out of the layout and detail.

tolerance.description: Per-channel difference a pixel must exceed to count as changed (0..=255).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_recording_show
tools.description: Read a HAR capture offline: requests, methods, statuses, hosts, timings and an API surface grouped by method + origin + path template, with JSON bodies reduced to outlines (no values). Cookies, credential headers, URL user-info and credential-like query values are never kept; secrets the caller names are redacted in raw, URL-encoded and JSON-escaped forms. Paged (offset/limit) or pick entries with record_numbers.

hidden_values.description: Values to redact wherever they appear (tokens, emails, ids). Only their count is recorded.

path.description: Absolute path of the capture file.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_scripts_save
tools.description: Write the scripts held by a web capture (page inspection or walkthrough evidence, a capture JSON file, or a HAR with saved bodies) into a new folder as files/<host>/<path> plus manifest.json; query variants and collisions get content-hash names with a stated reason. The result names the folder to pass to js_app_map.

capture.description: Capture evidence (inline or {"kind":"saved","evidence_id":...}) whose result lists scripts with url and source.

capture_path.description: Or an absolute path to a capture JSON file or a HAR file.

output_directory.description: Absolute path of a folder that does not exist yet.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_site_capture
tools.description: Record the open website into a new folder: full-page PNG screenshots at each requested width, the rendered HTML, design tokens (fonts, sizes, weights, text and background colours as hex, radii, shadows, spacing, content widths, CSS custom properties), the widths its CSS switches layout at, the layout at each width (page width, heading and text sizes, each section's padding, gap, content column and items per row), a layout outline of visible landmarks, headings, controls and images with positions, asset lists (images, stylesheets, scripts, font files, the requests it made), links and form outlines (never values). Writes capture.json and a README.md summary.

max_height.description: Tallest screenshot in CSS pixels; longer pages are cut here (600..=20000, default 12000).

noise_pass.description:
Photograph each width a second time a moment later and save the parts that changed by
themselves (carousels, videos, animations) as noise-<width>.png, white where it changed,
so comparisons can leave them out (default false).

output_directory.description: Absolute path of a folder that does not exist yet; the capture is written there.

widths.description: Page widths to screenshot, in CSS pixels (1..=4 widths, each 320..=3840). Default: desktop and phone.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_site_close
tools.description: Close the private browser started by web_site_open and delete its temporary profile.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_site_open
tools.description: Load a web page (http/https) in a private browser owned by this session (fresh profile, no history or logins) at a chosen window size, wait for it to finish loading, and report its final address, title and size. Every browser tool then inspects this page unless given another endpoint. Runs the site's scripts, so it needs your approval.

headless.description: Run the browser without a window (default true).

height.description: Window height in CSS pixels (320..=4000, default 900).

settle_ms.description: Extra time to let late content settle after the load event, in milliseconds (default 2000).

url.description: The page to open (http or https).

width.description: Window width in CSS pixels (320..=3840, default 1440).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_snapshots_compare
tools.description: Compare two web_page_show captures (frame origins, elements, resources, endpoints and script URLs added or removed), or two web_walkthrough_record runs step by step (steps aligned by step_id, then position: action, status, URL, error and artifact changes; network requests; event counts). normalization lists plain text replacements (e.g. a build id) applied to both sides first. Pure computation over evidence; no browser.

before.description: The earlier capture: web_page_show / web_page_watch evidence (inline or retained).

normalization.description:
Exact-literal replacements applied to every text value of both sides before comparing, in
rule_id order (at most 100), so volatile values such as build ids don't count as changes.

match.description: The exact text to replace (no patterns).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_standin_build
tools.description: Read a network recording (.har) of the original site and write standin.json into a folder: its routes (method and path template, with ids as {id}), and for each the status codes, content types, query names and a bounded set of recorded answers. It's for giving a rebuilt front end something to talk to. Credential headers, cookies and secret-shaped values are dropped and counted; pages, scripts and pictures are left out unless include_static is set. It only knows what was recorded. Returns a summary and a page of routes.

hidden_values.description: Values to drop wherever they appear, in every encoding (emails, ids, tokens). Only their count is recorded.

include_static.description: Also keep pages, scripts, styles, pictures, fonts and media.

# AGENTS.md

Rules for agents in this repo. **This file is only what you would get wrong by guessing.**
Elsewhere: `PROJECT_TREE.md` = "change X → start here" (read it first, before searching);
`PLANNING.md` = how to plan; `DESKTOP.md` = installer/tester runbook; `DEPLOY.md` = hosted ops.
Desktop mixer / mix-tab UX research: `docs/research/moises/REFERENCE.md` (Moises.app 2.0.3,
static only — do not clone it). Desktop Home parity plan: `docs/plans/moises-parity/10-MOISES-UI-CRAFT.md`
§13 and `11-DESKTOP-UI-REDESIGN.md` §12 (Phase 1.5; not implemented). Home uses measured Moises
geometry and Home-scoped neutrals. Do not change global theme tokens or the mixer palette for that
work. Do not copy Moises artwork, font files, or markup.

## Two products, one shared engine

- **Desktop** (local): Streamlit `ui/` behind `packaging/launcher.py`. Audio Isolation
  (separate/mix), YouTube to MP3 (save file only), Tab PDF. No Docker. Isolate jobs are
  **serial** — one at a time, 8–16 GB RAM (`ui/isolate_jobs.py`).
- **Website** (hosted): FastAPI `backend/` + React `web/` + Caddy; jobs via
  Postgres/Redis/MinIO + arq worker (`docker-compose.yml`). **Streamlit is not in this
  stack** — `Dockerfile` copies only `src/`, `backend/`, `scripts/`.
- **Shared**: `src/audio_to_tab/` (import as `audio_to_tab`). Engine changes can break
  either product; test both affected surfaces.

### The two "Lites" are different products — never unify
- Desktop **Interface Lite** = Streamlit chrome (`ui_mode` sidebar) that auto-profiles
  speed/device (`audio_to_tab.hardware.lite_auto_choice`) and the guitar engine
  (`ui/isolate_state.py` `resolve_lite_guitar_engine`); Pro exposes every control.
- Hosted processing mode **`lite`** = "Lite / low RAM" in `backend/capabilities.py`,
  hard-capped by API quota (60 s). Not the same thing (`docs/ui-issues.md` I-609).
- Desktop Lite must **not** silently clamp audio length; hosted `lite` **does**
  (`docs/issues.md` I-500).
- YouTube to MP3 is download-only and never affects speed/device; Pro only widens the
  export-format list and help copy.

## Python

- **3.10–3.12 only** (Basic Pitch needs <3.13). `.python-version` = 3.11.
- Dev/test venv `.venv311`; desktop freeze uses a separate `.venv-desktop*`.
- `make install` → `pip install -e ".[dev,eval,demucs,roformer,separator,analysis]"` (+ CPU torch
  on Linux). The **desktop** freeze install is a different profile — `README.md`.
- `make` delegates to `scripts/dev.sh` / `scripts/dev.ps1`; edit those, not the Makefile,
  when adding a target.

## Commands

`make <target>` (POSIX) or `.\scripts\dev.ps1 <target>` (Windows). `make help` lists all.

| What | Command |
|---|---|
| test | `make test` → `pytest tests/ -q` (1030 tests) |
| one test / file | `python -m pytest tests/test_metronome.py -q` · `::test_name` · `-k expr` |
| lint | `ruff check src/audio_to_tab` |
| backend | `make backend` (uvicorn `:8000`) |
| SPA dev | `make web` (Vite `:5173`, proxies `/v1` → `:8000`) |
| SPA test / build | `cd web && npm test` (vitest) · `make web-build` (build **+** vitest) |
| Streamlit | `make ui` (local demo only) |
| prewarm / fixtures | `make preflight` · `make tester` · `make fixtures` |

- `PYTHONPATH` is `src:.`, exported by the Makefile; `tests/conftest.py` also injects
  `src/` + repo root, so bare `pytest` works.
- **Lint covers `src/audio_to_tab` only** — not `ui/`, `backend/`, `web/`. ruff pinned
  `==0.16.5` (matches `.venv311`). `E501` ignored (100 cols advisory);
  `BLE001`/`S110`/`S112`/`RUF001-003` ignored project-wide.
- **No typecheck gate anywhere.** `web/tsconfig.json` is `strict` with
  `noUnusedLocals`/`noUnusedParameters`, but `vite build` never runs `tsc` and CI never
  does either. Run `cd web && npx tsc --noEmit` yourself before calling TS work done.
- **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, every push/PR) runs only pytest + ruff.** It does not
  run `npm test`, does not typecheck, does not build the desktop frontends.

## Committed frontend builds — edit source, rebuild, commit

Three Streamlit iframe components ship **hashed Vite output committed to git** so
installer testers need no Node. Never hand-edit `frontend/build/`.

| Component | Source | Rebuild |
|---|---|---|
| `ui/stem_mixer_component/frontend/` — live mixer (`main.ts`, `metronomeClicks.ts`) | `frontend/src/` | `make mixer-build` |
| `ui/region_picker_component/frontend/` — wavesurfer region picker | `frontend/src/` | `make region-picker-build` |
| `ui/mix_tabs_component/frontend/` — Moises-style Home\|mix\|+ strip | `frontend/src/` | `make mix-tabs-build` |

- **pytest enforces this.** `tests/test_stem_mixer_component.py`,
  `test_region_picker_component.py`, `test_mix_tabs_component.py` each assert the
  committed build is complete. Edit `src/` and forget the rebuild → red tests.
  `desktop-release.yml` also fails the release if the mixer build is missing.
- These three have **no test script** (no vitest). Only `web/` does.

## Invariants — do not "fix" these

- **MPS only at ≥12 GB RAM** (`MPS_MIN_RAM_GB`, `src/audio_to_tab/hardware.py`; pinned by
  `tests/test_hardware.py::test_mac_mps_gated_behind_12gb_ram`). Below that,
  unified-memory OOM/swap is worse than CPU. Do not raise
  `PYTORCH_MPS_HIGH_WATERMARK_RATIO` to "fix" an 8 GB Mac.
- **Desktop isolation is GPU-first** when CUDA or eligible MPS exists; memory pressure
  picks speed/quality, it no longer downgrades device to CPU. The 8 GB Mac CPU floor stays.
- **Metronome contract:** `MetronomeResult.click_times_1x` — defined in
  `audio_to_tab/metronome.py`, consumed by the desktop mixer. `rebake_metronome_artifact`
  reloads the stored grid and re-renders; it must **not** re-track. Tracking is a
  `librosa.feature.tempo(aggregate=None)` curve (librosa 0.11 spelling;
  older versions used `librosa.feature.rhythm.tempo`) → a second
  `librosa.beat.beat_track(bpm=curve)`.
- **Mixer background play:** `installWakeHooks` acts only on `visible`/`pageshow`/`focus`
  and never soft-pauses on document hide. Kept in sync between
  `ui/stem_mixer_component/frontend/src/main.ts` and `web/src/mixer/engine.ts` — change
  one, change the other. Browsers suspending Web Audio on a fully backgrounded tab is
  accepted, not a bug.
- **Mixer export is built on "Save current mix"**, not on every mute/solo/volume change
  (`docs/ui-issues.md` I-607).
- **Model weights download via SHA256-pinned `urllib`**, never `huggingface_hub`
  (`tests/test_guitar_ft_weights.py`).
- **Never reuse or renumber issue IDs.** `docs/issues.md` and `docs/ui-issues.md` reserve
  `I-072`, `I-098`, `I-104`, `I-200`–`I-252`, `I-500`–`I-510`, `I-618`, `I-600`–`I-623`
  (CI and eval scripts cite them). Append new sections; next UI ID is `I-624`.
  Many rows are `implemented-in-code` history — **read the code before treating a row as
  an open gap.**

## Desktop / packaging

- `AUDIO_TOOLS_EDITION` = `cpu` | `cuda` | `both` (aliases `nvidia`/`gpu`,
  `combined`/`cpu+cuda`/`all`); resolved by `src/audio_to_tab/edition.py` plus
  `packaging/edition.txt` inside the freeze. `desktop-release.yml` asserts `edition.txt`
  matches the env var.
- `make desktop-bundle-ffmpeg` (writes gitignored `packaging/ffmpeg/current`) is
  **required** before `make desktop-build`.
- Desktop onedir **must not** contain `backend/`, `web/`, or any `.env*` — asserted by
  `desktop-release.yml` and excluded in `packaging/audio_tools.spec`. Don't add hosted
  code to the spec.
- Releases are tag-triggered (`desktop-v*`) or `workflow_dispatch`, producing 4 **unsigned**
  artifacts (win cpu / win cuda / mac arm64 / mac x64). Version lives in
  `src/audio_to_tab/__init__.py` `__version__` — bump it there, not in the spec.

## Testing quirks

- Most tests mock torch/demucs, but `tests/test_tab.py::test_is_demucs_available` asserts a
  **real** Demucs import. A `[dev]`-only install fails — use the `make install` profile.
- YouTube integration tests skip unless `RUN_YOUTUBE_INTEGRATION=1` (public internet).
- Tests needing `eval/fixtures/*.mid` **skip** when missing — run `make fixtures` if you
  see unexpected skips rather than assuming they passed.
- macOS CI deselects `tests/test_api.py::test_upload_and_job` (basic-pitch has no
  TensorFlow wheel on Darwin). Not a bug to fix; Windows/Linux run it.
- Backend work: set `ATT_REQUIRE_AUTH=false` locally. The `starlette.testclient` →
  `httpx2` deprecation warning is pre-existing noise.

## Env / config

- All settings are `ATT_*` in `backend/config.py`. Copy `.env.example` (hosted),
  `.env.lite.example` (lite compose), or `web/.env.example` (SPA) → `.env`.
  **Never commit `.env`.**
- Demo mode: `ATT_DEMO_MODE=true` + `ATT_REQUIRE_AUTH=false` → per-tab anonymous JWT.
- CORS: exact origins in `ATT_CORS_ORIGINS`, **never `*`**. Production refuses placeholder
  `ATT_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and needs a strong `ATT_SECRET_KEY`.
  `ATT_ALLOW_YOUTUBE` defaults **off** (keep off on public hosts).
- `.streamlit/config.toml` sets `fileWatcherType = "none"` and `headless = true` — after
  editing `ui/`, **restart Streamlit**. That is expected, not a bug.

## Never commit / never hand-edit

- `.env`, `data/`, `output/`, wavs (except `eval/fixtures/*.wav`), model weights,
  `packaging/ffmpeg/`, `dist/`, `build/`.
- `web/dist/`, every `node_modules/`, every `*/frontend/build/assets/*` (hashed output).
- `.cursor/`, `CONTEXT_TREE.md`, `docs/oracle-free-memory-spike.md` — gitignored internal
  docs. `PROJECT_TREE.md` is the tracked canonical tree; update it when adding files.
- Streamlit gotchas: `st.expander()` takes no `help=` kwarg (use `st.caption()` inside);
  every interaction re-runs the whole script, so state handling is the app's real problem.

## Git

Do not commit, push, tag, or open a PR unless the user explicitly approves it in that
conversation.

# PROJECT_TREE

## How to use this file

Agents (including Continue / local LLMs): read this before searching the repo. Pick a path from the table, then open that file.
Humans: map of where desktop vs website vs shared engine live.
How to run: `DESKTOP.md` (local Streamlit / installer) or `DEPLOY.md` (hosted compose). Not this file.
If a path is not listed, it was not on disk when this was written (see **Last verified**).

## Two products

Both products import `src/audio_to_tab/` (isolate, YouTube ingest, tab PDF pipeline). They do **not** share UI or job runners.

1. **Desktop (local only)** — Streamlit `ui/app.py` behind `packaging/launcher.py`. Boot page is **Home** (`ui/pages/home.py`); then Audio Isolation (separate/mix), YouTube to MP3 (save file only), Tab PDF (demo), Settings. Serial isolate jobs in-process (`ui/isolate_jobs.py`). No Docker.
   - **Lite / Pro** here means Streamlit **interface mode** (`ui_mode` in sidebar): mainly shapes **Audio Isolation** (and Tab PDF Pro gates). Lite shows goal outcome cards and auto-profiles speed/device/guitar from RAM/GPU (`audio_to_tab/hardware.py`, `prefer_roformer` gated on accelerator); Pro exposes every stem/engine/diagnostic control. **YouTube to MP3 ignores Lite/Pro.** Wiring: `ui/app.py`, `ui/isolate_state.py`, `ui/pages/isolate.py` / `tab_pdf.py`. Testers: `DESKTOP.md`.
2. **Website (hosted)** — FastAPI `backend/` + React `web/` + Caddy. Jobs via Postgres/Redis/MinIO + arq worker (`docker-compose.yml`). Streamlit is **not** in that stack.
   - Hosted processing modes Auto / `lite` / fast_cpu / etc. live in `backend/capabilities.py`. **That “lite” is not desktop Interface Lite.** Operators: `DEPLOY.md`.

Shared: isolate engine, mixer math (`src/audio_to_tab/mixer.py`), ingest, tab pipeline.
Not shared: Streamlit pages vs React pages; desktop disk queue vs API `JobManager`; desktop iframe mixer vs website Web Audio mixer (same wake/background-play policy in both). The desktop mixer also shows a synced picture (YouTube or a local source video) and can resize stem waveforms while that picture is visible. The website mixer is audio-only.

## Guitar isolation status (important context)

The engine supports several guitar isolation backends, behind optional extras
(`[demucs]`, `[roformer]`, `[separator]`, `[scnet]`) and SHA256-pinned urllib downloads (no `huggingface_hub`):

- **HTDemucs-6s** (stock) and **htdemucs-6s-guitar-ft** in-process (`separate.py`).
- **BS-RoFormer-SW** (6-stem) and **MelBand-RoFormer Guitar** specialist (`roformer.py`).
- **SCNet** (`guitar_scnet`) — optional 4-stem MUSDB18 model; guitar content is in `other` (`scnet.py`). Opt-in, not the default first-stage separator.
- Post-processing: **fold-other** (incl. adaptive fold / bleed gate / ensemble paths — see `tests/test_guitar_improvements.py`), **bass-bleed diagnostics + opt-in HPF mitigation**, **low-end recovery**, **guitar pre-refine vs refined variants**, **lead/rhythm split** (not default).

The **Tab PDF path (`pipeline.py`) and the Isolate path (`isolate.py`)** are both wired for Demucs/RoFormer/refine/debleed/restore; SCNet is isolate/CLI-facing. Desktop UI (`tab_pdf.py`, `isolate.py`) and website/API (`backend/contracts.py`, `main.py`, `jobs/runner.py`) expose the guitar option fields they support.

## If you need to change X, start here

| Job | Start here |
|-----|------------|
| Isolation UI (desktop) | `ui/pages/isolate.py` (page: Home\|mix\|+ strip, Queue below), `ui/isolate_state.py` (Lite outcomes / Pro stems / progress / mode helpers), `ui/opened_audio.py` (OS open-with queue), `ui/app.py` (Lite↔Pro sidebar + overlay), `ui/stem_icons.py` (outcome/stem icons). **Separate/mix** — not download-only. |
| Desktop Home / UI craft (Phase 1.5) | Current Home: `ui/pages/home.py` (clean Home by default; `AUDIO_TOOLS_UI_V2=0` keeps the old page). Shell chrome is shared across desktop pages from `ui/app.py` + `ui/design_tokens.py` (navy `#192542`, blue `#2A4467`, amber `#F6AD49`; do not retint `ui/theme_presets.py`). Component: `ui/home_component/` (`make home-build`). Measurements: `docs/plans/moises-parity/10-MOISES-UI-CRAFT.md` §13. Tasks: `11-DESKTOP-UI-REDESIGN.md` §12. |
| Desktop Lite↔Pro mode | `ui/app.py` (sidebar `UI_MODE_*`, `load_ui_mode` / `write_ui_mode`), `ui/isolate_state.py` (`is_pro_mode`, `DEFAULT_UI_MODE`). Branching: Isolation `ui/pages/isolate.py`; Tab PDF Pro gates in `ui/pages/tab_pdf.py`. YouTube to MP3 does not read Lite/Pro. |
| Lite outcome cards | `ui/isolate_state.py` (`OUTCOME_CARDS`, `resolve_outcome_card`, `outcome_card_for_options`), icons `ui/stem_icons.py`, render in `ui/pages/isolate.py` |
| Desktop Lite hardware auto | `src/audio_to_tab/hardware.py` (`lite_auto_choice`, `lite_auto_speed_id`, `lite_accelerator_available`, Detected/Using captions; GPU-first when CUDA/MPS available; MPS ≥12 GB). Wired in `ui/pages/isolate.py`; guitar preference via `prefer_roformer` in `ui/isolate_state.py`. Hosted Auto is separate: `backend/capabilities.py` |

Live click-track Accent/rate/sound on the metronome row (hot-swap; no full stem reload). **Background play:** `installWakeHooks` recovers on visible/pageshow only — does **not** soft-pause on document hide. Loader: `ui/stem_mixer_component/__init__.py` (`youtube_video_id`, `local_video_url`, `video_offset_sec`, `hide_youtube_video`). Preview encode: `ui/media.py`. Outputs per run: `analysis.json`, `analysis_diagnostics.json`, `chart.musicxml`, `chart.txt`, `tab/transcription.{tab,pdf,mid}`, `tab/tab.json`, `project.json`. Chord `confidence` is the top-two softmax gap. |
| Region picker (desktop iframe) | Edit `ui/region_picker_component/frontend/src/main.ts` + `style.css`, then `make region-picker-build`. Loader: `ui/region_picker_component/__init__.py`. Wired in `ui/pages/isolate.py` (`_render_region_controls`) |
| Mix tabs (desktop iframe) | Edit `ui/mix_tabs_component/frontend/src/main.ts` + `style.css`, then `make mix-tabs-build`. Loader: `ui/mix_tabs_component/__init__.py`. Moises-style Home\|mix\|+ strip on Isolate |
| Mixer picture (desktop) | YouTube iframe or local `source_video` beside the stems, synced to mixer time. Wiring: `ui/pages/isolate.py`, `ui/isolate_state.py` (`mixer_youtube_video_id`, `mixer_local_video_path`, `prefer_local_mixer_picture`), offset `ui/isolate_jobs.py` (`video_offset_sec_for_run`), preview file `download_youtube_preview_video` in `src/audio_to_tab/ingest.py`. In the iframe: move/resize, snaps left/right/above/below, free-float (`videoLayout` in `sessionStorage`). Local file is tried first and can fall back to the YouTube id. |
| Stem wave height (desktop, picture visible) | Drag `#btn-resize-stems` on `#stems` while a picture is showing (not hidden). `stemWaveHeight` default 52, clamp 32–120, `sessionStorage` key `audiotools_stem_mixer_stem_wave`. CSS `--stem-wave-height` on `.waveform-svg` (metro waves scale with it). Handle hides with the picture. Does not change seek, mute/solo, or video layout. Tests: `tests/test_stem_mixer_component.py`. |
| Live mixer (website) | `web/src/mixer/engine.ts`, `web/src/mixer/pan.ts`, `web/src/components/StemMixer.tsx` — same wake/background-play policy as desktop; Media Session + `keepPlaying` across blur (blur is not Pause). Pan uses the same law as desktop `pan.ts`. No picture. Tests: `web/src/mixer/engine.test.ts`, `web/src/mixer/pan.test.ts` |
| Metronome click stem | `src/audio_to_tab/metronome.py` (adaptive tempo curve + local `beat_track`; `click_times_1x` / optional `bpm_curve` diagnostics; rebake). Desktop attach/wiring: `ui/pages/isolate.py`. Live options: mixer `metronomeClicks.ts`. Tests: `tests/test_metronome.py` |
| YouTube ingest | `src/audio_to_tab/ingest.py` (shared: `download_youtube_audio`, `download_youtube_preview_video`, `search_youtube_videos`, `is_youtube_url`, `format_youtube_duration`). Surfaces: `ui/pages/isolate.py`, `ui/pages/youtube_audio.py`, `ui/pages/tab_pdf.py`. Hosted SPA has **no** YouTube UI. `POST /v1/jobs` accepts `youtube_url` only if `allow_youtube` (`backend/config.py`, `backend/main.py`); default off. `POST /v1/isolate/jobs` is upload-based. Tests: `tests/test_ingest.py` |

## Tree

### Root files

Bleed-gate / adaptive fold / ensemble covered in tests `test_guitar_improvements.py`.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_builds_line_up
tools.description: Pair the functions of two builds of a program (two absolute paths) with the built-in engine. In order: unique names that aren't generated; Rust names with the compiler's hashes left out (a crate's hash changes with the toolchain); identical bytes; bytes with addresses masked out; a structural fingerprint of block count, called names and referenced strings. Each pair says how it was matched, with what confidence, and what comparing the bodies found: a pair by name is still reported as changed when its code differs. Candidates that can't be told apart stay unpaired and are listed as ambiguous. Lists are paged together (offset/limit); show picks one; detail=summary keeps every row for core_evidence_browse. Nothing is executed. Takes as long as analysing both programs.

tools.description: Make a game-ready, low-poly 3D model (GLB) with fal.ai (Tripo P1) and save it inside app/. Give a prompt (a picture is made first, then turned into the model) or an image (a web address, or a picture inside the project such as reference/picture-1.png). faces caps the face count (48 to 20000, default 3000): about 500-1500 for small props and pickups, 2000-5000 for weapons, furniture and vehicles, 6000-15000 for main characters; fewer faces run faster, so use the fewest that still look right. textured (default true) gives colours and surfaces. tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_publisher_show
tools.description: Read a Windows program's Authenticode signature block: each certificate table entry, the signer's subject, issuer, serial and validity dates, every embedded certificate, and the digest algorithm. Checks what the file alone can show: its hash against the signed hash, the signature against the embedded signer certificate, and how the embedded certificates link. Uses the active target unless path is given.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_rizin_command_run
tools.description: Run one read-only Rizin command against a file (absolute path or the active target) with user settings and scripts disabled (`rizin -N -q -c <command> <file>`; the file is opened read-only). Commands are checked against an allow-list of read-only families: information (i...), printing and disassembly (p..., x...), analysis (a...), search (/...), seek (s...), flags (f...), comments (C...), types (t...) and help (?...). Shell escapes, writes, file opening, debugging, scripts, configuration changes, pipes, redirects and command chaining are refused. Returns the raw text paged by lines. Optional engine.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_rizin_session_begin

Returns a session_id for native_rizin_session_command_run, native_rizin_session_show and native_rizin_session_end, plus Rizin's start-up messages. The program's own console output isn't captured. Sessions live in memory for this run; at most 4 at a time. Starting a program or attaching to one asks for consent.

tools.description: Summarize a saved pcap or pcapng capture with the built-in decoder (nothing installed): format, interfaces and link types, packet and byte counts, time span, frames per protocol, busiest addresses, conversations (flows) with packets and bytes in each direction and the application protocols seen (paged), DNS questions and answers, HTTP/1.x requests (method, Host, target; credentials removed) and TLS ClientHello server names (SNI) and ALPN. Values that change every run (process ids, loopback ports, 10 ms time buckets; optionally paths and literal patterns) are normalised so two runs compare. Bounded by time, output and files; the whole process group is killed on timeout or cancel. Runs code, so it needs your OK.

schema.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_walkthrough_record
schema.description: Run a program under a terminal with a scripted timeline of typed input, resizes and signals, then record the terminal screen, exit, and (opt-in) which files changed. environment.description: Extra environment variables applied on top of the inherited environment.

finish_ms.description: 0 = SIGKILL at the deadline; > 0 = SIGTERM, wait this long, then SIGKILL.

Make two runs comparable: replace values that change every run (on by default for process

time_step_ms.description: Round event dispatch times down to this many milliseconds (0 keeps them exact).

3	## How to use this file
4	
5	Agents (including Continue / local LLMs): read this before searching the repo. Pick a path from the table, then open that file.
6	Humans: map of where desktop vs website vs shared engine live.
7	How to run: `DESKTOP.md` (local Streamlit / installer) or `DEPLOY.md` (hosted compose). Not this file.
8	If a path is not listed, it was not on disk when this was written (see **Last verified**).
9	
10	## Two products
11	
12	Both products import `src/audio_to_tab/` (isolate, YouTube ingest, tab PDF pipeline). They do **not** share UI or job runners.
13	
14	1. **Desktop (local only)** — Streamlit `ui/app.py` behind `packaging/launcher.py`. Boot page is **Home** (`ui/pages/home.py`); then Audio Isolation (separate/mix), YouTube to MP3 (save file only), Tab PDF (demo), Settings. Serial isolate jobs in-process (`ui/isolate_jobs.py`). No Docker.
15	   - **Lite / Pro** here means Streamlit **interface mode** (`ui_mode` in sidebar): mainly shapes **Audio Isolation** (and Tab PDF Pro gates). Lite shows goal outcome cards and auto-profiles speed/device/guitar from RAM/GPU (`audio_to_tab/hardware.py`, `prefer_roformer` gated on accelerator); Pro exposes every stem/engine/diagnostic control. **YouTube to MP3 ignores Lite/Pro.** Wiring: `ui/app.py`, `ui/isolate_state.py`, `ui/pages/isolate.py` / `tab_pdf.py`. Testers: `DESKTOP.md`.
16	2. **Website (hosted)** — FastAPI `backend/` + React `web/` + Caddy. Jobs via Postgres/Redis/MinIO + arq worker (`docker-compose.yml`). Streamlit is **not** in that stack.
17	   - Hosted processing modes Auto / `lite` / fast_cpu / etc. live in `backend/capabilities.py`. **That “lite” is not desktop Interface Lite.** Operators: `DEPLOY.md`.
18	
19	Shared: isolate engine, mixer math (`src/audio_to_tab/mixer.py`), ingest, tab pipeline.
20	Not shared: Streamlit pages vs React pages; desktop disk queue vs API `JobManager`; desktop iframe mixer vs website Web Audio mixer (same wake/background-play policy in both). The desktop mixer also shows a synced picture (YouTube or a local source video) and can resize stem waveforms while that picture is visible. The website mixer is audio-only.
21	
22	## Guitar isolation status (important context)
23	
24	The engine supports several guitar isolation backends, behind optional extras
25	(`[demucs]`, `[roformer]`, `[separator]`, `[scnet]`) and SHA256-pinned urllib downloads (no `huggingface_hub`):
26	
27	- **HTDemucs-6s** (stock) and **htdemucs-6s-guitar-ft** in-process (`separate.py`).
28	- **BS-RoFormer-SW** (6-stem) and **MelBand-RoFormer Guitar** specialist (`roformer.py`).
29	- **SCNet** (`guitar_scnet`) — optional 4-stem MUSDB18 model; guitar content is in `other` (`scnet.py`). Opt-in, not the default first-stage separator.
30	- Post-processing: **fold-other** (incl. adaptive fold / bleed gate / ensemble paths — see `tests/test_guitar_improvements.py`), **bass-bleed diagnostics + opt-in HPF mitigation**, **low-end recovery**, **guitar pre-refine vs refined variants**, **lead/rhythm split** (not default).
